image_description: A close-up, high-angle shot of a sea lion resting on a rocky surface. The animal's head is tucked down against its body/flipper, obscuring the face and eyes. The fur appears thick, coarse, and light brown/tan, with visible texture. A small external ear flap is visible on the side of the head. The background consists of dark, textured rock.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head is angled downward and tucked into the body, making the top of the skull (sagittal crest) invisible from this perspective.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: External ear pinnae (visible ear flaps) distinguish from true seals.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: A distinct, small, fleshy ear flap is clearly visible on the side of the head, confirming it is an eared seal (otariid) and not a true seal.
Stiff, light-colored whiskers are visible protruding from the snout area, although the very tip of the nose is slightly out of frame/focus.
